caption: The video captures a close-up of several translucent icicles hanging from a beige gutter edge. A band of white snow runs along the top right, and a dark teal surface fills the left and lower background. The icicles themselves stay fixed, their banded glassy bodies catching the light without changing shape. The main visible motion is a continuous dripping cycle, as small droplets appear at or below the tips and fall through the dark area. Near the start, a pair of droplets descends below the central icicles, then separate droplets fall through the left and lower right portions of the view. The dripping keeps an irregular rhythm, with droplets forming glossy bulges at the points and dropping through the middle of the dark area. Tiny droplets vanish near the lower edge, while a slight camera drift shifts how much gutter shows at top. The process runs throughout, with no clear beginning or end shown.
relations: Water accumulating at the fixed icicle tips -> droplets form glossy bulges and detach downward.
Detached droplets falling through the dark background -> the continuous dripping cycle persists irregularly.
The banded glassy icicle bodies remaining fixed -> their overall shape persists during the dripping process.
